open_points.subject: A08 rule 7 binding acceptance re-check scope
open_points.text: "a `proposed` one is read against the manifest as rule 6 does and, when a check fails — in the order rule 5 lists them..."; rule 6 excludes instance checks ("not those of the instance, which are A09 rule 6's own").
open_points.question: When accepting a proposed binding, must the kernel re-run only rule 6's manifest-record checks, or the full rule 5 list including instance-selection/api_base_url/required_headers checks?
options: Re-check only record/digest/invocability checks from rule 6
Re-check full rule 5 mismatch sequence including instance checks
open_points.default_guess: Re-check only rule 6 record-level checks, because rule 7 says "as rule 6 does" and send-time instance checks are assigned to A09 rule 6.

open_points.subject: A10 rule 7 request_digest header set
open_points.text: "the request an approval covers is described... by ... every header the kernel sends"
open_points.question: Does "every header the kernel sends" include transport/library-added on-wire headers (e.g., Host, Content-Length, User-Agent), or only headers explicitly set by kernel logic?
options: Digest only kernel-declared headers (required headers, credential header name, and explicitly set protocol headers)
Digest all headers that appear on the wire after HTTP client processing
open_points.default_guess: Digest only headers explicitly constructed by kernel logic.

open_points.subject: A10 rule 7 with multipart/form-data boundary
open_points.text: "for `multipart/form-data` ... the parts ... so the boundary is not part of it" together with "every header ... each with its value"
open_points.question: How is approval stability guaranteed for multipart requests if Content-Type includes a boundary value that may change per send?
options: Boundary must be deterministic for identical logical request
Boundary parameter must be normalized/omitted in the header portion used for request_digest
Boundary may vary, forcing re-approval on each changed digest
open_points.default_guess: Normalize Content-Type for digest purposes (exclude boundary parameter) so identical logical multipart requests keep the same request_digest.

open_points.subject: A12 start-input validation on `many` ports
open_points.text: "each value, in port name order, fits its port's schema... for a `many` port, is a JSON array whose every element fits it"
open_points.question: If multiple elements in the same `many` input fail schema/size checks, which one must be reported as the refusal cause?
open_points.default_guess: Report the first failing element by index for determinism.

open_points.subject: A04 trial-case validation on `many` inputs/outputs
open_points.text: "ports taken in name order and, for one port, presence, carriage, schema, then size"
open_points.question: For a `many` port where several list elements violate schema/size, what deterministic sub-order picks the named failure?
options: Element index order within the list, first failing element named
Report port-level failure without element specificity
open_points.default_guess: Use element index order and name the first failing element.
